rows.label: Output
rows.note: Where the sound goes. Over HDMI the sound is not bit-perfect; HDMI has no volume control of its own, so its volume is Software or Fixed, and the visualiser moves only on Software.
rows.warn: Playback stops while the output changes.

rows.label: Sound card board
rows.note: Most boards and every USB DAC are found by themselves. A board that is not - it does not show under Output - can be chosen here.
rows.warn: Choosing a board restarts the player with it. If no sound card appears after the restart, the player goes back to what it had and restarts again.

rows.label: Volume
rows.note: How the level is set. Hardware: by the sound card's own volume control, bit-perfect at every level. Software: by the player recalculating the sound - for an output with no volume control of its own, such as HDMI; not bit-perfect below 100 %. Fixed: always full level, for an amplifier that sets the volume itself; the change applies when playback next stops.

warn.Software: The player changes the level by recalculating the sound. Playback is no longer bit-perfect, at any volume below 100 %. Use it for an output with no volume control of its own, such as HDMI, or if you prefer it. Hardware restores bit-perfect playback.
warn.Fixed: Fixed output sends the signal at 100%. Turn your amplifier down before confirming — the panel can no longer lower it.

rows.label: Maximum volume
rows.note: The loudest the player will go, on any input. Set it to 80 and the player is never louder than the slider at 80 — and 100% on the panel, in LMS and on a connected phone all mean that level, so no control shows a number louder than what comes out.

rows.label: Volume-managed renderers
rows.note: Bluetooth excluded pending Finding 006.

rows.label: Volume curve
rows.note: How the slider's travel maps to loudness, over 60 dB either way. Cubic is the shape a volume control usually has — half travel is −15.5 dB. Linear spreads the decibels evenly instead, which puts half travel at −30 dB and makes the bottom of the slider very quiet.

rows.label: Server
rows.note: Servers announce themselves on the network. Typing an address is the fallback, not the route.
rows.empty: No servers found. Check the server is running, or enter its address by hand.

rows.label: Extended navigation
rows.note: Lyrion's own menus on the home screen: My Music, Favourites, Apps, and what the apps add.

rows.label: Plugins
rows.note: Superseded by the Plugins category, which George asked for on 2026-09-25. ADR-0022 inventoried this as a row in Sources; what it would have opened is now a category of its own, listing each installed plugin's switch. Kept unsurfaced rather than deleted because removing an inventoried row is George's call.

rows.label: Starting volume
rows.note: The loudest Spotify starts at when it takes over, whatever its app was last set to. A lower level stays where it is; a higher one comes down to this.

rows.label: Advertised name
rows.note: Follows the device name.

rows.label: Pairing
rows.note: Confirmation shows a six-digit code on the panel and waits for it to be accepted. PIN-free pairs anything in range without asking.

rows.label: Trusted devices
rows.note: View and forget remembered devices. Clearing breaks automatic reconnection.
rows.empty: No devices paired yet. Pair one from your phone's Bluetooth settings while the player is discoverable.

rows.label: Auto-trust on pair
rows.note: Remembers a device once its pairing is confirmed, so it reconnects on its own. Off means every connection is a fresh pair.

rows.label: Re-anchor seek position
rows.note: Pressing play on a deactivated player currently loses the position entirely.

rows.label: Reclaim LMS when a session ends
rows.note: When Spotify, Bluetooth or Plexamp stops, Lyrion takes the player back. A phone that locks can end a Spotify session, and switch the player to Lyrion without warning.

rows.label: Release ladder
rows.note: Polite stop, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL.

rows.label: Transition screen length
rows.note: How long the takeover animation stays up. It is shown on every takeover, however quick; a takeover still in flight when this runs out keeps it up until it finishes.

rows.label: Attached screen
rows.note: Sets the layout, Standard or Bar, and which visualiser skins are offered.
rows.warn: Changing it restarts the player on the new screen. If that changes the picture, the screen asks whether to keep it, and without a touch on Keep within 2 minutes it goes back.

rows.label: Screen rotation
rows.note: For a screen mounted the other way up.
rows.warn: Changing it restarts the player and asks Keep this rotation? on the panel. If nobody touches Keep within 2 minutes, it goes back.

rows.label: Headless
rows.note: Turns the player's screen off. Every setting that only affects the screen is hidden while this is on.

rows.label: Show volume when changed elsewhere
rows.note: A phone’s volume change opens the drawer; the panel’s own changes do not.

rows.label: Volume drawer auto-hide
rows.note: When a change from elsewhere opened it.

rows.label: Phone touchpad
rows.note: A touchpad in the phone's volume sheet that moves a pointer on this screen, taps, types into its text fields, scrolls with two fingers and zooms with a pinch.

rows.label: Pointer speed
rows.note: How far the pointer moves for a finger's movement on the phone.

rows.label: Pointer style
rows.note: How the pointer the phone moves looks on this screen.

rows.label: Home screen list
rows.note: What the home screen shows.

rows.label: Screen
rows.note: The built-in screen shows the clock and weather. An external page loads the URL provided.

rows.label: URL
rows.note: External and lazy loaded. Falls back to the built-in screen when unreachable, unconfigured, or refusing to be framed.

rows.label: Timeout
rows.note: One timeout on every screen, counted while nothing is playing and nobody touches the panel.

rows.label: Background
rows.note: Artist pictures come from the library. Online wallpapers come from Pixabay and need a key. On-device wallpapers are read from local storage.

rows.label: Background brightness
rows.note: Brightness of the background picture. Recommended: 62%.

rows.label: Change the picture every
rows.note: How often the background changes — artist pictures, online wallpapers and the player's own.

rows.label: Pixabay API key
rows.note: A Pixabay key, from a free account. Use one per player to avoid throttling.

rows.label: Pexels API key
rows.note: A Pexels key, from a free account. With both keys, pictures come from both.

rows.label: Wallpaper topics
rows.note: Pixabay's own categories. Each new picture is drawn from one of the chosen ones at random, so several stay mixed rather than taking turns.

rows.label: Clock
rows.note: The time and the date, over the background.

rows.label: Weather
rows.note: Forecasts come from Open-Meteo.

rows.label: Location
rows.note: A city or place name. It can be changed at any time.

rows.label: Forecast
rows.note: Today's weather is always shown. 3 days adds a three-day forecast beside it.

rows.label: Timeout
rows.note: How long music plays before the visualiser takes the screen, counted from the last tap or skip.

rows.label: Stop when nothing is playing
rows.note: How long silence lasts before the visualiser gives the screen back.

rows.label: Skin type
rows.note: The kind of skin the visualiser picks from.

rows.label: Skin
rows.note: Which one the visualiser draws. Tapping a skin shows it; nothing changes until Use this skin.

rows.label: Spectrum smoothing
rows.note: Recommended: 90%. How much of each bar’s previous height is kept on every update. Low is twitchy, high glides and blunts a drum hit. Measured at 44.1 kHz: 50 settles in about 30 ms, 90 in 200 ms, 97 in 0.7 s. Applying it reopens the sound card, so it stops whatever is playing.
rows.warn: Changing this stops whatever is playing while the sound card is reopened.

rows.label: Needle fall time
rows.note: Recommended: 400 ms. How long a needle takes to drop from full scale to nothing. Its rise is immediate and cannot be slowed. Applying it reopens the sound card, so it stops whatever is playing.
rows.warn: Changing this stops whatever is playing while the sound card is reopened.

rows.label: Needle smoothing
rows.note: Recommended: 240 ms. How long a stretch of the music each needle is averaged over. Short twitches with every beat, long is a real VU movement and arrives late. Rounded to the nearest 40 ms, which is how often the meter reads its level. The visualiser restarts to apply it.

rows.label: Animate turntables and tapes
rows.note: The record turns and the tonearm follows the track; the reels of a cassette or a tape recorder turn. Off, they are drawn still.

rows.label: Record speed
rows.note: How fast a turntable's record turns. The skins are drawn for 33; a tape's reels keep their own speed.

rows.label: Rotation
rows.note: Stepped redraws a turning record or reel eight times a second. Smooth redraws it every frame it moves, at the expense of more CPU usage.

rows.label: Look up missing artwork
rows.note: For renderers that supply none.

rows.label: ListenBrainz token
rows.note: For the artist page's Popular list. A free user token, from https://listenbrainz.org/settings/

rows.label: fanart.tv key
rows.note: Artist pictures from fanart.tv. Without a key they come from the Lyrion server's Music & Artist Information plugin, or initials where it is not installed.

rows.label: TheAudioDB key
rows.note: Artist pictures and album covers where fanart.tv has none. Optional: without a key of your own, TheAudioDB's free shared key is used.

rows.label: Confidence threshold
rows.note: Recommended: 90%. How sure MusicBrainz has to be that it found the right artist or release. Below it the picture is not taken and LMS's is kept. It gates every enrichment lookup, not only pictures — a confidently wrong biography is worse than a blank panel.

rows.label: Find portraits and covers
rows.note: Looks up every album artist's portrait and every album's cover on fanart.tv, then TheAudioDB, and keeps LMS's picture where neither has one. Starts from scratch every time and checks all of them. Runs in the background; playback is not interrupted. What it found stays here until the next run.

rows.label: Device name
rows.note: One name for everything: the mDNS hostname, the LMS player, the Spotify Connect device and the Bluetooth name. There is no per-service override.
rows.warn: Changing it will restart the device.

rows.label: Wi-Fi
rows.empty: No networks found. Check the adapter is enabled, or move closer to the router.
rows.hint: A secured network needs its password the first time. Saved networks join in one tap.

rows.label: Time zone
rows.note: Taken from the network. Set it by hand only when that comes out wrong.

rows.label: Restrict API to loopback
rows.note: The API binds all interfaces and is unauthenticated by decision.

rows.label: Reboot
rows.note: Restarts the device. Playback stops.

label: Plugins
subtitle: What is installed beyond the player itself

rows.label: Visualiser skins
rows.note: The meters and spectra drawn for this screen's size. Off removes them, and the visualiser with them.

rows.label: Change logs
rows.note: What changed in the last 10 releases.

rows.label: Check now
rows.note: Reads this device's channel for a newer release. Installs nothing. ADR-0110: the Release tile's button and the update modal run it; not a row of its own.

rows.label: Update now
rows.note: ADR-0110: started from the update modal, which asks before stopping playback. Downloads, backs up, stops playback, installs, restarts the player and checks it; goes back to this release if the new one fails.

rows.label: Updates
rows.note: Automatic installs a waiting release at night, never while playing, and does not retry one that failed.

rows.label: Update channel
rows.note: Testing gets each release first. Stable gets it once it has been tried. Recommended: Stable.

warn.Testing: Testing releases reach this player before everyone else's, and may have problems. Going back to Stable does not downgrade: the player stays where it is until Stable passes it.

rows.label: Image build
rows.note: Nothing else on a running device reports which build it is.

rows.label: Back up now
rows.note: Writes the settings, the library's pictures, the paired devices and this device's own configuration into the Backups share.

rows.label: Restore
rows.note: Replaces everything a backup holds and restarts the device. Backups are read from the Backups share, so one copied there from another machine is offered too.
rows.empty: No backups yet. Back up first, or copy one into the Backups share.

rows.label: Debug logs
rows.note: Keeps the device's logs on the card across restarts, up to 100 MB, for tracking down a problem. Off, they are kept in memory and lost at a restart, and switching off deletes the ones kept. On by default on the Testing channel.

rows.label: Problem report
rows.note: Downloads the player's logs, versions, hardware and settings in one file, to attach to a report of a problem. Addresses, names, networks, shares, keys and what you play are taken out on the player first, but read the file before sharing it.

rows.label: Hardware feedback
rows.note: Tells the project how this sound card and screen work, so others can see what works before buying. Two short checks - the screen, then the sound - and a few questions, then feedback on GitHub, filled in with what the player reads of the hardware - never a serial number or anything about you.

rows.label: Factory reset
rows.note: Every setting returns to its shipped default. Paired devices and Wi-Fi credentials are cleared.

rows.label: Legal
rows.note: The player's licence, the licences of everything it is built from, and what it is not responsible for.

rows.label: Credits
rows.note: Everyone whose work is in the player.
